standard_prerequisites.name: Picard and cohomology under base change
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-change-fields-pic; Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology
standard_prerequisites.use: Injects Pic(X) into Pic(X_{overline{k}}) and preserves dim H^1 under the field base change, reducing to the algebraically closed case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reduction to the reduced curve
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology, Proposition cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian; Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma pic-lemma-torsion-descends
standard_prerequisites.use: The reduction surjection stays surjective on H^1 by Cech vanishing, and X_red to X is an isomorphism on components and on l-torsion of Picard groups.

standard_prerequisites.name: The reduced-proper torsion proposition
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final bound dim Pic(X)[ell] <= dim H^1(O_X) + g_geom for reduced proper curves over algebraically closed fields.

core_obligations: Base-change reduction (proof lines 3968-3975): Pic injects into the geometric Picard group and dim H^1 is preserved by flat base change, so k may be taken algebraically closed.

Reduction to X_red (proof lines 3977-3986): the surjection O_X -> O_{X_red} induces a surjection on H^1 since quasi-coherent cohomology vanishes in degree >= 2; the reduction is an isomorphism on geometric components and on l-torsion of Picard groups, so X may be replaced by X_red, reducing to the reduced-proper torsion proposition.
proof_roadmap: Descend to the algebraically closed field using Picard injectivity and H^1 base change.
Replace X by its reduction using the surjection on H^1 and the torsion isomorphism.
Apply the reduced-proper torsion proposition to conclude the bound.
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the l-torsion dimension of the Picard group of a proper curve by dim H^1(O_X) plus the geometric genus (statement lines 3959-3966). The proof (lines 3968-3986) is a complete two-step reduction: to the algebraically closed base via Picard injectivity and flat base change, then to the reduced curve via the Cech-vanishing surjection and the torsion-descent isomorphism, finishing with the reduced-proper proposition. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: systematic reductions with correctly ordered hinges.
